# Trident — Claude Code Operating Manual

> **This file is guidance only. All enforcement is handled by scripts.**
> Claude must call scripts instead of relying on memory of rules.
>
> Key enforcement scripts:
> - `ai-autopilot-preflight.sh` — hard pre-Gemini gate (roadmap, architect exit, paths, integrity)
> - `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` — pre-implementation gate (artifacts, state, UI, API)
> - `ai-validate-stage-artifacts.sh` — artifact existence + template compliance
> - `ai-promote-autopilot-artifacts.sh` — exports → canonical promotion
> - `ai-validate-ui-contracts.sh` — UI contract enforcement
> - `ai-validate-stac.sh` — Stac JSON compliance + binding validation (Gate C.3–C.6)
> - `ai-contract-validate.sh` — cross-repo contract validation
> - `ai-flow-validate.sh` — end-to-end flow validation
>
> **Stac invariant:** Never write `.stac.json` files directly. Use `ai-stac-generate.sh` which reads
> `.ai/bindings/screen_api_map.yaml` and enforces data source determinism.

---

## Enforcement Map

**Rule:** If Claude's shortcut can break production → script or hook. If shortcut only affects quality → skill is fine.

| Layer | Responsibility | Examples |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| **Claude thinks** | Creative/judgment work | Specs, plans, exploration, debugging, review, architecture |
| **Scripts enforce** | Mechanical/risky actions | `ai-stac-generate.sh`, `ai-stac-promote.sh`, `ai-stac-from-figma.sh`, `ai-theme-apply.sh`, `ai-variant-map-apply.sh`, all `ai-validate-*.sh`, `ai-stage-complete.sh` |
| **Hooks protect** | Forbidden mutations | `block-state-json-direct-write.sh`, `block-protected-paths.sh` |
| **Human decides** | Irreversible/risky choices | Stage approval, contract changes, PR review |

**Protected paths** (hook-enforced, blocked on Write/Edit):
- `.ai/contracts/screen_patterns/*.yaml` — frozen blueprints
- `.ai/stac/kits/*/` — frozen component mappings
- `contracts/ui/component_selection_rules.yaml` — frozen selection logic
- `.ai/themes/*.yaml` — must use `ai-theme-apply.sh`
- `contracts/screen_variant_mapping.yaml` — must use `ai-variant-map-apply.sh`
- `.ai/stages/*/ui_reference_manifest.yaml` — approval is sanctioned-writer-only (`ai-ui-source-approve.sh`); a Builder must not self-approve (BQ3, epic mobile-ui-source-integrity)

**Override:** Set `ALLOW_PROTECTED_PATH_EDIT=true` for dedicated contract stages.

---

## 0b) Advisor Usage (manual — decision-heavy phases only)

> The Claude Code **Advisor** (a second model the main model consults for a strategic second
> opinion, e.g. Fable 5) is **not** wired into the engine and is **not** always-on. It is a harness
> setting (`/advisor`), toggled **manually by the human**. Advisor tokens are additive (they burn
> plan usage faster), so use it where judgment matters and keep it off for mechanical work.

**Turn Advisor ON for decision-heavy phases:**
- exploration
- epic architecture
- stage planning
- go/no-go
- security/payment risk review
- production readiness decisions

**Keep Advisor OFF for mechanical phases:**
- implementation
- test fixing
- formatting
- routine verification
- branch cleanup

**Why not always-on:** advisor calls are additive token cost; leaving it on during implementation
loops burns usage with no quality gain. **When to enable:** manually, at the start of a
planning/spec/gate/decision session. **When to keep off:** during `ai auto` implementation, test
fixing, and routine verification. **Do NOT auto-toggle** the advisor from hooks/scripts unless
Claude Code confirms per-phase toggling is supported — treat it as a human-controlled setting.
This is guidance only: it changes **no** `ai auto` execution behavior.

---

## 0c) Roadmap Alignment (lightweight operating rule — no enforcement)

> Guidance only. No script, no gate. A 30-second check Claude runs **before starting
> net-new implementation work** — not before executing already-approved plan items.
> Purpose: prevent roadmap drift and infinite local optimization. Default bias:
> **roadmap progress over local perfection.**

**Run only on net-new intent** — an ask that is *not* already a line in the approved
spec/plan ("also add X", "while we're here, refactor Y", "should we handle Z"), or the
kickoff of a new stage/epic. Do **not** run it per-file, per-edit, or on test/format/verify.

**Identify (from existing sources — no new artifacts):**
- Current Epic → `.ai/epics/<id>/state.json`
- Current Stage → `CURRENT_STAGE.md`
- Exit Criteria → spec **Acceptance Criteria (AC-ids)** + epic `conformance.matrix`

**Classify the request (exactly one):**

| Class | Meaning | Action |
|-------|---------|--------|
| **A** Required now | already in the approved plan | proceed |
| **B** Required for stage exit | maps to an **unmet AC**, not yet planned | proceed + amend plan |
| **C** Improvement | quality gain, no AC depends on it | **do not auto-implement** → backlog candidate |
| **D** Future roadmap item | belongs to a later stage/epic | **do not auto-implement** → backlog candidate |
| **E** Drift | maps to **no** AC of any planned stage | **do not auto-implement** → backlog candidate / `orphanWork` |

**For C/D/E:** stop, state the class, record it as a backlog candidate in `.ai/decisions/`
(and drift as `orphanWork` via `ai-epic-state.sh`). Do not open a branch or write code.

**If context is missing** (no `CURRENT_STAGE.md`, no spec ACs): the only valid outcome is
**HOLD** — surface the gap, do not execute.

**When all exit criteria are satisfied:** recommend closing the stage and selecting the
**next roadmap objective** — do not keep polishing the current one.

**One-line rule of thumb:** *If it doesn't close an exit criterion, it doesn't run now —
it gets recorded.*

### 0c.1) Close-time audits (operating rule — no enforcement)

> Extends §0c. Guidance only. Two audits Claude performs **before recommending a
> close** — reading signals that already exist, not building new ones. The lesson
> behind this: a green banner is not proof (the ADMIN-SEM failure — every step green,
> journey broken).

**Before closing a STAGE — audit mutation paths for bypasses:**
- Every state/contract change went through its **sanctioned writer**, not a hand-edit:
  - `.ai/epics/<id>/state.json` → only via `ai-epic-state.sh`
  - stage `state.json` → only via `create_state_json()`
  - themes / variant maps / `.stac.json` → only via `ai-theme-apply.sh` /
    `ai-variant-map-apply.sh` / `ai-stac-generate.sh`
  - protected paths (§ Protected paths) → not edited with `ALLOW_PROTECTED_PATH_EDIT`
    left on past its stage
- Check the git history of those files: a change authored by a hand-edit rather than a
  script, or a hook override (`ALLOW_*=true`) still active, is a **bypass** → stop and
  reconcile before closing.
- Modified files ⊆ plan (scope holds).

**Before closing an EPIC — verify exit criteria are objectively met:**
- Every stage's Acceptance Criteria are `PASS` in `conformance.matrix` — **read the
  matrix, do not infer from tests passing.**
- `orphanWork` is **empty**. Any remaining item is either backlogged (§0c) or blocks the
  close — it is never silently dropped.
- Epic-done conditions hold: all stages `done`, all active seams `PASS`, Epic-QA verdict
  `PASS` (and Epic-QA did not judge its own artifact).

**If any check fails:** the stage/epic **stays open**. Record the gap; do not close on a
green banner.

This is guidance only: it changes **no** `ai auto` execution behavior.

---

## 0d) Proactive Status on Stop (universal — report-only)

> Guidance only. **Report-only, not a gate.** Generalizes §13.2's Operational Status heartbeat
> beyond the Epic Owner: the same proactive status applies to **any** Engine-controlled workflow that
> auto-progresses — Epic Owner (§13), `/autopilot`, exploration (`/explore-run`), workstream — so the
> user never has to ASK "why did it stop?"

**Trigger.** Whenever such a workflow transitions from automatic execution to **requiring human
action** — a declined or blocked tool call, a hook rejection, a `WAITING_FOR_HUMAN` / `BLOCKED` /
human-gate state, or an unrecoverable error — it **immediately** surfaces a concise operational
status, **without waiting to be asked**. A declined tool permission is a harness/session event (no
Engine script runs), which is exactly why this is a prompt-contract rule rather than a script gate.

**Format — reuse §13.2, do not fork it.** The heartbeat is §13.2's **six fields**
(Current status / Active agent / Current blocker / Next automatic action / Human action required /
Queue); §13.2 is the format authority and there is **no parallel format**. Per OWN-3, the **body
above** the heartbeat carries, on a stop:
- current lifecycle/phase,
- the last attempted action,
- the result/reason execution stopped,
- whether anything was changed or lost,
- the exact human action required,
- the next automatic action after the human resolves it.

**Report-only — no new gate.** This rule **reports**, it does not gate. It requires **no
acknowledgement**, adds **no new §13.7 gate**, and does **not** change §13.2.1 automatic progression:
auto-progression on non-stop transitions is unchanged, and the status fires only **on a stop that has
already occurred** — it never introduces a pause of its own.

**Objective trigger (prose class, mirroring §13.2).** A workflow that transitions to requiring human
action and does **not** immediately surface this status — leaving the user to ask "why did it stop?"
— is in violation.

## 0) Engine Mode: Lean vs Governance

The engine operates in one of two modes, set in `.ai/config/project.conf`:

```bash
ENGINE_MODE=lean        # default — speed, minimal ceremony
ENGINE_MODE=governance  # opt-in — full multi-agent pipeline, strict enforcement
```

Per-stage override: `STAGE_37_10_MODE=governance` (dots become underscores).

### Lean Mode (default)

| Aspect | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| Spec/plan author | Claude |
| Reviewer | Human (you say "go" or "change X") |
| Enforcement | Spec exists, plan exists, scope guard, tests pass |
| Templates | Required as structure, major sections checked, human decides quality |
| Artifacts | Written directly to `.ai/specs/`, `.ai/plans/` |
| Commands | `ai epic create`, `ai build`, `ai done` *(Phase 2 — not yet implemented)* |

**Lean chain of command:**
1. **Claude** writes spec + plan
2. **Human** approves (or requests changes)
3. **Claude** implements
4. **Human** reviews diff + tests pass

**Lean enforcement (scripts still run, with reduced checks):**
- `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` → checks spec exists, plan exists, ROADMAP tracking
- `ai-autopilot-preflight.sh` → skipped (no Gemini gate)
- `ai-promote-autopilot-artifacts.sh` → skipped (direct write)
- `ai-validate-stage-artifacts.sh` → checks existence + basic section count
- `ai-validate-template-sync.sh` → skipped (no strict template compliance)

**Optional reviewer in lean mode:**
```bash
ai review <stage> --gemini     # request Gemini review on demand
ai build <stage> --mode governance  # escalate one stage to governance
```

### Governance Mode

Full multi-agent pipeline. All gates active. Use for:
- High-risk stages (auth, payments, data migration)
- Cross-repo boundary changes
- Compliance-sensitive work

**Governance chain of command:**
1. **Architect (ChatGPT)** defines scope + acceptance criteria + file list
2. **Gatekeeper (Gemini)** approves spec before implementation
3. **Claude Code** implements ONLY the approved spec
4. **Reviewers (Gemini + ChatGPT)** review implementation

### Mode Detection

All scripts use `read_engine_mode()` / `is_lean_mode()` / `is_governance_mode()` from `ai-common.sh`.
Resolution order: per-stage override → repo-level `ENGINE_MODE` → default `lean`.

If spec is missing/ambiguous: **STOP and ask.**

## 1) Ownership Model

**Engine repo** owns: scripts, templates, commands, prompts, validators, gate profiles.
**Target repos** own: stage artifacts, contracts, decisions, config, roadmap, **project-specific Stac artifacts** (screen patterns, kits, themes, theme registry, supported widgets, pattern overrides, variant mappings).

### Engine vs Target Artifact Boundary

Engine owns HOW to validate/generate/manage artifacts (tooling).
Target repo owns WHAT artifacts exist for that product (data).

| Artifact | Owner | Path |
|----------|-------|------|
| Screen patterns | Target repo | `.ai/contracts/screen_patterns/` |
| Nucleus kit mappings | Target repo | `.ai/stac/kits/nucleus_v1/` |
| Theme files | Target repo | `.ai/themes/` |
| Theme registry schema | Target repo | `.ai/contracts/theme_registry.yaml` |
| Supported widgets | Target repo | `.ai/contracts/stac_supported_widgets.yaml` |
| Pattern override schema | Target repo | `.ai/contracts/pattern_override_schema.yaml` |
| Variant mapping | Target repo | `.ai/contracts/stac_variant_mapping.yaml` |
| Validators/generators | Engine | `scripts/ai-validate-*.sh`, `scripts/ai-stac-*.sh` |
| Templates | Engine | `.ai/templates/` |
| Commands | Engine | `.claude/commands/` |

Engine validators use `resolve_project_artifact()` to find artifacts in the target repo first, with engine fallback + warning.

Forbidden in target repos: `.ai/templates/`, `.ai/commands/`, `scripts/ai-*.sh`.
Run `ai doctor` to check.

### Canonical Entrypoints

| Action | Script | Scope |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Stage registration | `ai-stage-seed.sh` | ROADMAP + CURRENT_STAGE only. No specs, no artifacts. |
| Stage execution | `ai auto` (autopilot) | Sole entry point: spec → review → implement → done |
| Architect consultation | `ai-architect.sh` | Spec/plan generation, design questions |
| Quick question | `ai-ask.sh` | Mid-execution Q&A, reviewer |
| Pre-Gemini preflight | `ai-autopilot-preflight.sh` | Hard gate: roadmap, exit code, paths, integrity |
| Artifact promotion | `ai-promote-autopilot-artifacts.sh` | exports/ → canonical paths (called by autopilot) |
| Execution | `ai-run.sh --stage-execute` | Legacy execution path |
| Prompt loading | `load_prompt()` in `ai-common.sh` | |
| State creation | `create_state_json()` in `ai-common.sh` | |
| Template resolution | `resolve_template()` in `ai-common.sh` | |

**Core invariant:** No command except `ai auto` may generate or promote implementation artifacts.
`ai stage seed` is a lightweight registrar. `ai explore` is a thinking phase. All execution goes through autopilot.

### Autopilot Seed Ownership Contract

| Responsibility | Owner | What it does NOT do |
|----------------|-------|---------------------|
| Stage registration (ROADMAP + CURRENT_STAGE) | `ai-stage-seed.sh` | Does NOT generate specs, does NOT call ChatGPT |
| Spec/plan generation | `ai auto` → `ai-architect.sh --plan --no-seed-prompt` | Does NOT register stages |
| Artifact integrity gate | `ai-validate-artifact-integrity.sh` | Runs BEFORE Gemini, BEFORE exports are trusted |
| Promotion to canonical paths | `ai-promote-autopilot-artifacts.sh` | Only runs AFTER Gemini GO verdict |

**Enforcement:** `ai-architect.sh` auto-detects autopilot context via `AUTOPILOT_MODE` env var
and suppresses the interactive seed/reject prompt. If `ai-architect.sh` exits non-zero,
autopilot MUST stop — no exports written, no state created, no Gemini review.
Partial exports are deleted on failure.

---

## 2) Session Rules

### Scope Declaration (mandatory at session start)

```
Scope: [directories being modified]
Cross-repo impact: YES/NO
Boundary classification: [domain-only | internal | shared-api | shared-ui | cross-repo | event]
```

### One Stage Per Session

- Parallel stages = separate sessions
- Sequential stages = separate sessions
- Forbidden paths are hard boundaries — use spec, not code exploration
- Spec-first, not explore-first

### Closed-Loop Execution

Never pause to ask "shall I proceed?" — auto-continue until complete, max rounds, or error.

---

## 3) Git Discipline

- Branch naming: `feat/<short-name>` or `fix/<short-name>`
- Commit early and often
- Never force-push without human instruction
- Merge conflicts: STOP and report

---

## 4) Command Safety

### Never run destructive commands without human confirmation

`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fdx`, remote pushes.

### Architect Routing (which command to use)

| Need | Command | Why |
|------|---------|-----|
| Spec + plan generation (Phase A) | `ai architect --plan "topic"` | Loads templates, 12-20K context, artifact-ready output |
| Design question (full context) | `ai architect --full "question"` | 8-12K context, repo-aware |
| Quick architecture question | `ai architect "question"` | Light 4-8K context, advice only |
| Mid-execution question | `ai ask "question"` | Lightweight, no templates, keeps pipeline moving |
| Mid-execution + persist decision | `ai ask --save-decision "question"` | Saves to `.ai/decisions/` |
| Security/risk review | `ai ask --reviewer "question"` | Reviewer perspective |
| Formal checkpoint (scope change) | `ai architect request "topic"` | Produces `.ai/architect/decision_<topic>.md`, halts until resolved |

**Rule:** `ai ask` is for quick questions during implementation. `ai architect` is for anything that produces or informs artifacts (specs, plans, decisions).

### Other Delegation Commands

- `ai-memory.sh recall --type failure` — check past failures
- `ai-memory.sh record engine-defect "description"` — record engine bugs

### Embedded Architect Consultation

Auto-triggers when: multiple valid approaches + affects architecture/UX/API.
Does NOT trigger for: deterministic code, bug fixes, repo-grounded questions.

Flow: identify options → `ai architect "question"` → present unified answer → wait for human choice.

### Architect Checkpoint

Formal, persistent consultation for decisions that change scope/files/approach.
- Produces `.ai/architect/decision_<topic>.md`
- Halts implementation until resolved
- Check existing decisions before triggering new ones
- ALL decisions must be persisted as artifacts — never conversation-only

### Decision Enforcement Gate

Before generating stage artifacts: scan `.ai/architect/decision_*<topic>*.md`.
- Decision exists → seed from it directly. Do NOT re-call `ai ask`.
- Decision missing → use `ai architect` or trigger formal checkpoint.

---

## 5) Token Efficiency

### Repo Inspection Rules

- Default tools: Grep → Glob → Read (in that order)
- Max deep reads: 3-5 files per investigation
- Use scripts (`ai-validate-*`, `ai-sdui-audit`) for bulk analysis
- **DO NOT use Explore agents** for simple lookup or general questions
- Explore is blocked by hook — only allowed for `/explore-run` or `ALLOW_EXPLORE_AGENTS=true`

### Tool Priority: Grep → Glob → Read

Never spawn Explore for existence checks, repo inspection, or general questions.

### Budget Rule

If exploration:implementation ratio exceeds 3:1, stop exploring and start implementing.

### Response Rules

- Short confirmations only (changed files + status)
- No trailing summaries — the diff speaks
- No duplicate reads
- Verification output: status + duration + failures only
- Written artifacts: `updated <path>` + 3-line summary

---

## 6) Enforcement Gates (script-enforced)

These are NOT rules to memorize — they are scripts to run.

| Gate | Script | When |
|------|--------|------|
| Pre-Gemini preflight | `ai-autopilot-preflight.sh <stage> --architect-exit $?` | After architect, before Gemini |
| Template sync | `ai-validate-template-sync.sh` | During preflight (Check 13) |
| Pre-implementation | `ai-autopilot-guard.sh <stage> --phase D` | Before writing code |
| Artifact validation | `ai-validate-stage-artifacts.sh <stage>` | After promotion |
| UI contracts | `ai-validate-ui-contracts.sh` | UI stages |
| API boundary | `ai-autopilot-guard.sh <stage> --phase F` | Completion of API stages |
| Completion | `ai-autopilot-guard.sh <stage> --phase F` | Before marking done |

### What Scripts Check (you don't need to memorize)

- state.json exists with correct phase
- Canonical artifacts in `.ai/specs/`, `.ai/plans/`, `.ai/reviews/`, `.ai/implementations/`
- Nothing stuck in `.ai/exports/`
- Spec template sections present (derived from `spec_template.md`, not hardcoded)
- Template evidence exists (proves templates were read before generation)
- Template ↔ validator sync (no drift between template headings and validator checks)
- UI artifacts (if UI stage)
- API contracts (if shared boundary)
- Post-review exists (completion)

### Canonical Pipeline Path (the ONLY valid execution order)

```
ROADMAP → architect exit 0 → write exports
  → preflight gate → Gemini review → promote
  → implement → self-tests → post-review
```

Anything outside this path is a hard stop.

### Failed Output Rules (engine-enforced by preflight gate)

1. **Never continue from failed tool output.** If `ai-architect.sh` exits non-zero, its output is untrusted. Discard it entirely.
2. **Discard, don't patch.** If architect output is malformed, delete exports and re-run after fixing the cause. Never manually edit spec/plan to fix architect failures.
3. **No patching spec/plan after failed architect output.** The preflight gate (Check 8) detects when architect exited non-zero but exports exist — this means someone patched manually. Hard stop.
4. **Regenerate only after fixing the cause.** If architect fails because of missing context, wrong template, or bad prompt — fix that first, then re-run clean.

---

## 7) Artifact Flow

```
.ai/exports/  →  ai promote  →  .ai/specs/, .ai/plans/, .ai/reviews/, .ai/implementations/
                                  .ai/stages/${id}/state.json
```

- `.ai/exports/` = staging area, NEVER source of truth
- Phase C promotes → canonical paths
- Phase D reads from canonical paths ONLY
- `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` blocks if artifacts missing

---

## 8) Boundary Rules

When a stage creates shared APIs or contracts, the enforcement scripts check for required artifacts at completion. Run the guard with `--phase F` to verify.

Boundary types → required artifacts:
- Shared API → OpenAPI + consumer docs + contract manifest
- Shared UI → UI contract/schema
- Cross-repo → integration contract + ownership
- Event → event schema + producer/consumer contract
- SDUI changes → `.ai/contracts/registry_delta_<stage>.json`

---

## 9) SDK/API Grounding

Before writing SDK-dependent code: inspect pinned version → lockfile → local usage patterns → implement against pinned version. Never silently write code for a newer API.

---

## 10) Platform Verification

Run before post-review (scripts enforce this):
- Flutter: `flutter analyze` + `flutter test`
- Backend: `./gradlew clean build`
- Web: `npm run lint` + `npm run build`

If verification fails → CHANGES_NEEDED, not post-review.

---

## 11) Reviews & Packs

### Review Independence Invariant (GLOBAL)

**No agent may independently review an artifact it generated.**

| Phase | Author | Reviewers | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Phase B (brief review) | ChatGPT | Gemini + Claude | ChatGPT authored the brief |
| Phase D (plan review) | Claude | ChatGPT + Gemini | Claude authored the spec/plan |
| Phase G (post-review) | Claude | ChatGPT + Gemini | Claude implemented the code |

All review artifacts must include `ARTIFACT_AUTHOR:` and `REVIEWERS:` metadata.
Enforcement: `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` Gate 4e (review independence).

| Review | Owner | When |
|--------|-------|------|
| Conformance | Claude | Every stage |
| Boundary | Gemini | Cross-package work |
| Integration Gate | Claude | Multi-repo stages |
| Flow Validation | Claude | UI or cross-repo flows |
| Adversarial | Gemini + ChatGPT | Critical boundaries |

Optional packs (include when relevant): NFR, Security Audit, DevOps, ADR, Integration Gate, Evidence, UI Readiness, Flow Validation. Templates in `.ai/templates/`.

### Dual-Reviewer Decision Matrix

Only unanimous GO (plan review) or unanimous APPROVE (post-review) proceeds. All other combinations block.

| ChatGPT Verdict | Gemini Verdict | Pipeline Action |
|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| GO | GO | Proceed |
| GO | GO WITH CHANGES | BLOCK — patch + re-review |
| GO | NO-GO | BLOCK — fix issues |
| GO WITH CHANGES | Any | BLOCK — patch + re-review |
| NO-GO | Any | BLOCK — fix issues |
| APPROVE | APPROVE | Proceed (post-review) |
| Either CHANGES_NEEDED | Any | BLOCK — fix + re-review |
| Either REJECT | Any | BLOCK — fix + re-review |

Enforcement: `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` Gate 4d (plan review), Gate 4e (independence), and Gate 7a (post-review).

---

## 12) Definition of Done

Run `ai-autopilot-guard.sh <stage> --phase F` — it checks everything.

Additional human-verified items:
- No edits outside assigned scope
- Scope declaration matches actual changes
- PR summary: what/why, risks, tests run

---

## 13) Epic Owner Contract

> **Read this if you are the Epic Owner.** It is written for a session with **no transcript**.
> Everything an Owner needs in order to run the workflow is here or in a file named here; nothing
> is left to be remembered from a conversation.
>
> Established by bounded item **O7**. It **supersedes** `.claude/commands/epic-own.md`, which
> described a human-gated advisor that hands every decision back to the human. That description did
> not survive contact: the Owner dispatches Builders and Verifiers, manages bounded rework,
> escalates at a round cap, gates on independent proof and merges. The old file is retained with its
> history for the record; **this section is the live contract.**
>
> Changing this section is a **human decision** (see §13.7).

### 13.0 What the Owner is

**The Owner is a state machine, not a document writer.** It holds the position in the lifecycle,
decides the next action, and executes it. Its output is progress plus an honest status — never an
analysis that ends by handing the human a list of things to decide.

The failure this contract exists to prevent, observed directly: an Owner drifted from *managing* the
workflow to *reporting* it, and the human became the component that remembered what happens next.
That is the exact dependency the framework exists to remove.

**Governing constraint register:** `.ai/decisions/CARRY-FORWARD-REGISTER.md`. It is the authority on
every rule referenced by ID below. Read it at every stage transition; a transition performed without
consulting it is a process defect.

### 13.1 The lifecycle

```
prepare package → validate package → fix framework deficiencies → dispatch external Builder
  → review evidence → dispatch independent Verifier → classify findings (VER-1) with FIX/DEFER
  → manage bounded rework → escalate at the round cap (TERM-1) → gate ONLY on independent proof
  → merge (serialized) → update epic state via the sanctioned writer → select next objective
```

Each state below gives its **entry condition**, the Owner's **obligations** in it, its **exit
condition**, and the **next automatic action** — the thing the Owner does *without being asked* once
the exit condition holds. Where an exit needs the human, the state names exactly what the human
decides.

---

#### S1 — Prepare package

- **Entry condition:** an objective is selected and no Builder is active on it.
- **Obligations:** author a self-sufficient dispatch package — the defect or charter in one
  sentence; an explicit file allowlist; the acceptance criteria with objective triggers and required
  report format; **every applicable register row quoted verbatim, never cited by ID**; every file,
  commit and suite named by a path that resolves from a clean clone; the execution transport
  (`PROV-1`); the **complete** deliverables list; and the verifier contract. Resolve the stage's
  artifact set per §13.5 rather than enumerating it from memory — that omission is what happened to
  5.2.1.
- **Exit condition:** the package is written.
- **Next automatic action:** S2 — validate it. Never dispatch straight from S1.

#### S2 — Validate package

- **Entry condition:** a dispatch package exists.
- **Obligations:** run the gate, do not eyeball it:
  ```bash
  ai-epic-own.sh dispatch-check <epic> <stage>            # chartered stage
  ai-epic-own.sh dispatch-check <epic> <item> --package <path> --kind bounded
  ```
  It fails closed on an unresolved deictic reference, a register row cited but not quoted, an
  unresolvable file or commit, an unstated transport, and a deliverables list missing an artifact
  the done gate requires. It is a **validator**: it reads, it never repairs.
- **Exit condition:** exit 0. A non-zero exit is a defective package, which is the **Owner's**
  failure to fix (`OWN-1`), not a Builder's problem to discover.
- **Next automatic action:** on exit 0 → S4. On non-zero → fix the package and re-run S2.

#### S3 — Fix framework deficiencies

- **Entry condition:** a Builder or Verifier reports a `FRAMEWORK_DEFICIENCY`, or `dispatch-check`
  fails.
- **Obligations:** apply `OWN-1`. Missing information found **before** dispatch is an Owner failure.
  Missing information found **during** execution is a **framework deficiency by default**; it is
  reclassified as Builder error **only on evidence**, and the burden of proof sits with the claim of
  Builder error. Fix the dispatch package, then redispatch against the corrected package.
  **Never resolve a deficiency by asking the human for the missing input** — that converts a
  framework gap into a permanent human dependency. Reporting a gap is a contribution and is never
  counted against the agent that reported it.
- **Exit condition:** the package answers the gap and `dispatch-check` is green.
- **Next automatic action:** S4 — redispatch.

#### S4 — Dispatch external Builder

- **Entry condition:** `dispatch-check` green, and dispatching now stays within the `SEQ-2` cap of
  **two mutation-capable agents** (see §13.4 — verifiers count).
- **Obligations:** dispatch a **fresh** Builder session carrying the package and nothing else.
  State the execution transport in the record (`PROV-1`). Record the round ordinal — this is round 1
  unless it is rework.
- **Exit condition:** the Builder returns `READY_FOR_VERIFICATION` or `BLOCKED`.
- **Next automatic action:** `READY_FOR_VERIFICATION` → S5. `BLOCKED` → S3 if the block is a
  framework deficiency, otherwise §13.7 escalation.

#### S5 — Review evidence

- **Entry condition:** a Builder has returned.
- **Obligations:** read what the Builder produced, not what it claimed. Apply `L-7` — **never trust
  a producer's exit status, validate the produced document** — and `BANNER-1` — a proof must read
  *the comparison actually performed*, not a printed banner. Confirm the changeset is within the
  allowlist, diffed against the item's **own base via `git merge-base`**, never against a moving
  `main` (`SCOPE-2`).
- **Exit condition:** the deliverables exist and are internally coherent. This is a completeness
  check, **not** a verdict — the Owner does not verify its own dispatch.
- **Next automatic action:** S6. If deliverables are missing outright → S8 rework, counted as a
  round.

#### S5a — Milestone reviews (`MILESTONE-1`)

- **Entry condition:** the Builder reports a **milestone** — a phase, an AC group, or an artifact
  family — not an individual file or commit.
- **Obligations:** review the milestone against the **stage intent**, then publish a concise record.
  Four questions, no more:
  1. **Architectural drift** — does the shape being built still match the Core Invariant and the
     architecture block, or has it quietly become a different design?
  2. **Scope drift** — is the changeset still inside the allowlist, diffed against the item's own
     base (`SCOPE-2`)?
  3. **Acceptance coverage** — which ACs does this milestone now claim, and with what evidence?
     Which remain untouched?
  4. **Continue or correct** — `CONTINUE` unchanged, or a **bounded** correction naming exactly what
     to change.

  Publish to `.ai/stages/<id>/milestone_reviews.md`, appended. **Concise: a milestone review is
  supervision, not a verdict.**

- **Default cadence** (a stage may declare its own set in its dispatch package):

  `Planning → Contracts/schemas → Validators → Regression → Evidence → Ready for verification`

- **Exit condition:** a published review with `CONTINUE` or a bounded correction.
- **Next automatic action:** on `CONTINUE`, the Builder proceeds **automatically** — no human gate,
  no waiting. On a correction, the Builder applies exactly the named items and re-reports the same
  milestone. At `Ready for verification` → **S6**, dispatch the independent Verifier.

**Three constraints that keep this from becoming something it must not be:**

- **A milestone review is NOT verification and NEVER substitutes for it.** The Owner does not verify
  its own dispatch (§11 independence invariant). The independent Verifier's scope stays uncapped
  (`VER-2`) and is not narrowed by anything a milestone review already looked at.
- **A milestone review does not consume a `TERM-1` round**, and neither does a bounded correction
  issued from one. Rounds count rework cycles following an **independent verdict**. If milestone
  corrections consumed rounds, a stage would exhaust `TERM-1` before it ever reached verification.
- **Do not review every file or commit.** Per-commit review is what this section exists to replace;
  it interrupts Builder flow and buys nothing that verification does not buy better.

> **Implementation status — not yet mechanical.** Today a Builder is dispatched as one session that
> runs to completion, so there is no point at which it reports a milestone. Making this real requires
> the dispatch package to **declare its milestone set**, and the executor to dispatch **per
> milestone** — which also makes each milestone independently resumable from artifacts (`PORT-1`).
> Until then the cadence is honoured by dispatching milestone-scoped work, and any claim that
> milestone review is automatic would be false.

#### S6 — Dispatch independent Verifier

- **Entry condition:** S5 complete.
- **Obligations:** dispatch a **fresh** Verifier with no prior involvement in this item. The
  Verifier must never be the agent that produced the artifact (§11 independence invariant), and the
  Owner never verifies its own dispatch. Scope the verifier brief by item class:
  - **Chartered stage** → verification is **fully open and adversarial**. `VER-2`: *verification
    SCOPE must not be restricted for chartered stages.* Never cap it.
  - **Bounded item** → bounded verification per `.ai/decisions/BOUNDED-ITEM-CONTRACT.md`: reproduce
    the defect, verify the fix, attempt **exactly one** Owner-named adjacent bypass, run only the
    named suites. **The Owner must name that single bypass** — a verifier told to "attack it" will
    correctly attack everything.
- **Exit condition:** a verdict — `READY_FOR_GATE`, `REWORK_REQUIRED` or `BLOCKED`.
- **Next automatic action:** S7 — classify.

#### S7 — Classify findings (`VER-1`)

- **Entry condition:** a verdict exists.
- **Obligations:** classify **every** finding as `regression` / `same-defect-class` /
  `new-defect-class` / `architectural-observation` / `baseline-attribution` / `process-observation`,
  and record **FIX or DEFER with a one-line reason**. A DEFER that matters to a future stage becomes
  a **new register row with an objective trigger** — "remember to do this later" is not a mechanism.
  Record round ordinal, verifier identity, verdict and transport.
- **Exit condition:** every finding carries a class and a FIX/DEFER.
- **Next automatic action:** all FIX items empty and verdict `READY_FOR_GATE` → S9. Otherwise → S8.

#### S8 — Manage bounded rework

- **Entry condition:** the verdict is `REWORK_REQUIRED`, or S7 produced FIX items.
- **Obligations:** dispatch a rework round with **only** the FIX items in scope. A bounded item that
  grows past its directive is a **finding for the Owner, not work for the Builder**. Increment the
  round counter. **Re-scoping an acceptance criterion does NOT reset the counter** — otherwise
  `TERM-1` is bypassable by editing the criterion.
- **Exit condition:** the round returns, or the counter reaches the cap.
- **Next automatic action:** rounds 2 and 3 → back to S6 (fresh verifier). **Round 3 failing to
  discharge the outstanding criteria → S10, unconditionally.**

#### S9 — Gate

- **Entry condition:** an **independent** verdict of `READY_FOR_GATE`.
- **Obligations:** gate on the independent proof, never on the Builder's self-report and never on a
  green banner. Run the close-time audits in §0c.1. Gates are **strictly serialized** — one at a
  time, `SEQ-2`.
- **Exit condition:** the audits hold.
- **Next automatic action:** S11 — merge. If an audit fails, the stage **stays open**: → S8 or §13.7.

#### S10 — Escalate at the round cap (`TERM-1`)

- **Entry condition:** three Builder rounds have not discharged the criteria.
- **Obligations:** **stop the Builder workflow.** Do not order a fourth implementation round —
  specifically not because "convergence appears close", which is the failure mode this rule exists
  to stop. Produce the escalation record; **all five items, or the escalation is incomplete**:
  (1) total Builder rounds; (2) total verifier rounds; (3) unresolved acceptance criteria, named;
  (4) why round 3 did not converge; (5) classification of the remaining work as **implementation
  deficiency / acceptance-criteria deficiency / framework deficiency / architectural redesign**.
- **Exit condition:** **the human authorizes a fourth round, or re-scopes, or cancels.** This is a
  hard stop the Owner may not resolve itself.
- **Next automatic action:** on authorization → S8 as round **B4** (not a fresh budget of three; a
  failure at B4 escalates immediately). On re-scope → S1. On cancel → S12.

#### S11 — Merge and record

- **Entry condition:** gated at S9.
- **Obligations:** merge to `main`. **Merges are strictly serialized, one at a time** — the
  concurrent-merge incident this rule comes from merged another agent's in-progress branch. Re-check
  `HEAD` and the current branch immediately before every commit. Update epic state **only** through
  the sanctioned writer:
  ```bash
  ai-epic-state.sh ...          # never hand-edit .ai/epics/<id>/state.json
  ```
  Update the carry-forward register: mark rows the item discharged, add rows it produced.
  **Never delete a row** — discharged rows move to the Discharged table with the closing commit.
- **Exit condition:** merged, state written by the writer, register updated.
- **Next automatic action:** S12.

#### S12 — Select next objective

- **Entry condition:** the previous item reached a terminal state.
- **Obligations:** choose the next objective from the epic's dependency order and the register's
  sequencing rows. Apply §0c: if it does not close an exit criterion, it does not run now — it gets
  recorded.
- **Exit condition:** an objective is selected.
- **Next automatic action:** S1. **The loop does not pause here to ask permission for routine
  progression** — only the §13.7 hard stops pause it.

### 13.2 The Operational Status Contract (`OWN-2`, `OWN-3`) — mandatory

> **Operational Status is a heartbeat, not a report.**

**Every Owner response MUST end with this section.** No exceptions, including responses that are
mostly analysis. Its purpose is that a human controller, a Supervisor, or **a different AI session**
can read the execution state in **under 30 seconds without reading anything above it**. That is the
whole function. A status section that must be *studied* has already failed, however accurate it is.

**Canonical format — exactly these six fields, in this order, and nothing else:**

```
## Operational Status
Current status:          <one line: stage + what is happening right now>
Active agent:            Owner | Builder (external) | Verifier | None  — and what it is on
Current blocker:         None | <IDs only>
Next automatic action:   <single execution chain, e.g. Builder → Verifier → Gate → Merge>
Human action required:   None | <the decision, one line>
Queue:                   <next stages / milestones, arrow-separated>
```

**Worked example — this is the target shape:**

```
## Operational Status
Current status:          5.1.6 Round 2 — external Builder dispatched
Active agent:            Builder (external)
Current blocker:         None
Next automatic action:   Builder → Independent Verifier → Gate → Merge
Human action required:   None
Queue:                   5.2.2 → 5.2.3 → 5.2.4
```

**Rules — `OWN-3`:**

1. **Keep it under ~10 lines.** Six field lines plus the heading is the norm.
2. **Operational content only.** No root-cause analysis, no file paths, no `file:line` citations, no
   architecture reasoning, no recommendations, no evidence, no verdict rationale — **inside this
   section**.
3. **Blockers are IDs, never explanations.** `REWORK-1, DISPATCH-2` — not what they mean. The reader
   who needs the meaning reads the body or the register.
4. **`Next automatic action` is a chain, not a paragraph.** It answers *"what happens without me?"*
5. **Stable across every epic and every response.** The field names do not vary. A reader learns the
   shape once.
6. **Everything else goes ABOVE it, in its own sections.** New findings, framework deficiencies,
   technical analysis, verdicts, evidence and the Owner's recommendations are all body content that
   precedes the heartbeat. They are not deleted — they are relocated.

**What `OWN-3` does NOT repeal — the `OWN-2` non-transfer rule, relocated not removed:**

**A pending human decision still does not transfer the workflow to the human.** When
`Human action required` is anything other than `None`, the **body above** must carry, for each
decision, the Owner's **recommendation** and **the exact action sequence that fires on approval** —
so a single word resumes execution. `"Here are your options, let me know"` remains a contract
violation; `"I recommend X; on your 'go' I run A, then B, then C"` remains the required form. The
heartbeat names the decision in one line; the body carries its substance.

**Enforcement class: prose, and stated plainly rather than discovered later.** There is no validator
for this contract today — it sits in the same weak class as `VER-1`. Its objective trigger, for a
reviewer or a future checker: a response whose Operational Status section exceeds ~10 lines, omits or
renames a field, or contains a file path, a `file:line`, or the word "recommend" is in violation.

### 13.2.1 Automatic progression (`PROG-1`) — mandatory

> **`Human action required: None` is not a status. It is an instruction to the Owner to continue.**

**A completed agent result is an execution event, not a stopping point.** A verifier returning a
verdict, a Builder returning `READY_FOR_VERIFICATION`, a gate passing — none of these end the
Owner's turn. Each is an input to the next action, which the Owner takes **in the same control
cycle**.

**The Owner may stop for exactly four reasons, and no others:**

1. an explicit **human decision or approval** (the §13.7 list),
2. a **hard blocker** that physically prevents the next action,
3. **`TERM-1` exhaustion** — three Builder rounds spent without discharge,
4. a **mandatory safety or governance gate**.

**Anything else is a progression regression.** The Owner does not wait for "continue", "go ahead", or
"proceed"; it does not end a turn on an intention; and it never makes the human ask *why did you
stop*. Requiring that prompt is the same dependency `OWN-2` was written to remove, re-entering
through the schedule instead of through the reporting.

**Objective trigger, for a reviewer or a future checker:**

> If the last actor reached a **terminal** state, **and** the next action is known, **and** no human
> action is required, **and** no blocker exists — then the Owner **must dispatch that next action in
> the same control cycle.** A turn that ends in that state is in violation.

**Stage boundaries are transitions too (`PROG-2`).** `PROG-1` was first applied only *within* a
stage — Builder → Verifier → Gate — and the Owner still stopped at the boundary between stages, twice
reporting `Current blocker: None` / `Human action required: None` / `Next automatic action: seed the
next stage` and then waiting to be told. **A terminal `DONE` transition immediately triggers the next
queued stage in the same control cycle** when all of: the queue contains a ready stage; no blocker
exists; no human gate is required; and the epic is not complete. The expected flow is
`5.1.6 DONE → seed 5.2.2 → validate dispatch package → launch visible Builder`, with the human
receiving a status update **after** dispatch rather than being required to trigger it.

**Interaction with `OWN-3`, learned the hard way.** The `Next automatic action` field is a *promise
already kept*, never a plan. Writing "Next automatic action: Verifier → Gate → Merge" and then
ending the turn without dispatching the verifier turns the heartbeat into a substitute for the work.
Observed twice in one session: the Owner stalled after a verifier returned and again after
classifying its findings, and the human had to prompt both times.

### 13.3 The deficiency loop (`OWN-1`)

```
Builder hits a gap → is it missing documentation, or a genuine Builder error?
  → FRAMEWORK_DEFICIENCY by default (burden of proof is on the claim of Builder error)
  → fix the dispatch package → redispatch
```

**Never "ask the human"** for something the framework should have carried. The framework improves
only if gaps are attributed to it rather than to whoever tripped over them.

### 13.4 Rules the Owner inherits — carried here so they are not recalled

| ID | The rule, in operating terms |
|----|------------------------------|
| `VER-1` | Every finding gets a class and an Owner FIX/DEFER with a one-line reason. |
| `TERM-1` | **THREE Builder rounds** max per stage or bounded item; a fourth requires **explicit human authorization**. Re-scoping an AC does not reset the counter. |
| `FREEZE-1` | **Do not mutate a control-plane artifact while it governs an active execution.** Additive-only rows are permitted. Changing a live constraint requires **immediate re-dispatch** against the updated contract. This contract is never disjoint from an active stage — it is the thing running it — so contract work waits for a terminal state. |
| `PORT-1` | A stage must be executable by a fresh Builder from its artifacts alone. `PORT-1a` (structural) is enforced by `dispatch-check`. `PORT-1b` (behavioural replay) is **not yet testable** — see §13.6. |
| `SEQ-2` | **Two mutation-capable agents** maximum, and **verifiers count**. Every agent keeps writes in its own worktree, restores from saved copies rather than `git checkout`, and exits with `git status --porcelain` empty. Gates and merges stay strictly serialized. |
| `VER-2` | Verification **scope** is never capped for a chartered stage. |
| `L-7` | Never trust a producer's exit status — validate the produced document. |
| `BANNER-1` | A proof must read the comparison actually performed, not a printed banner. |
| `M-CF-2` | Never soften an existing rule or check to make work pass. Fix the artifact instead. |
| `SCOPE-2` | Scope proofs diff against the item's **own base** via `git merge-base`, never a moving tip. |
| `ATTRIB-1` | A register row asserting a live defect carries a reproduction command, and its actor is verified in code — not inferred from a trace. |
| `SHELL-1` | zsh is a supported **launcher**, not an interpreter: `zsh -c 'bash script.sh'`, never `zsh script.sh`. |

### 13.5 The canonical stage artifact model

**A stage does not enumerate its artifacts by hand.** The authority is
`.ai/contracts/artifact_registry.yaml`, which already declares, per artifact type, a `required`
class (`always` / `conditional` / `optional`) and an applicability predicate over
`stage_type` / `boundary` / `mode` / `touches_ui`. The Owner declares the stage's facts; the
registry selects the set.

**The mandatory core is derived from the done gate, not asserted.** `scripts/ai-epic-state.sh` fails
closed without:

| Artifact | Gate invariant | What the gate does without it |
|---|---|---|
| a canonical **spec** carrying `AC-<n>` ids, bound by sha256 | `I21` | `record missing spec binding … fail closed` |
| **verified evidence artifacts**, existing and hash-matched | `I16` | `no verified_evidence.artifacts to re-verify` |
| per-AC `evidence_ref` + an **independent** verifier | `I18` / `I19` | `verifier == owner — not independent` |

Lifecycle **state** is the single epic `state.json`, written only by `ai-epic-state.sh`. There is no
stage-local `state.json` — Stage 5.1.6.1 removed it deliberately, and re-adding one would resurrect
the dual-state-authority defect (`FINDING-F`).

Everything else is **selected, not mandated**: the registry's `conditional` rows apply when the
stage's predicate matches, and `optional` rows never block.

**`dispatch-check` enforces the gate-derived core and only advises on the rest.** Registry rows
marked `required: always` that a package does not name are reported as `WARN`. They are not failures
because expanding the enforced artifact set is **Stage 5.1.1's authority** and is gated behind the
unresolved `L-6` adoption decision — turning that gate on today would reject essentially every
existing artifact.

**Not this contract's to define:** the `verification_record` artifact type, its required-field schema
and its guard belong to **Stage 5.1.7.2**. This section states where verification evidence must
exist and what the gate requires of it; it deliberately does not specify its schema.

### 13.6 External Builder policy

Framework stages are executed by **fresh external Builder sessions** carrying only the dispatch
package. This is policy, not a per-dispatch choice, and it is why `PORT-1a` is enforced mechanically.

**Stated honestly:** no execution in this program has yet run through durable external dispatch.
Every one has been `OWNER_SUBAGENT` (`PROV-1`). **`PORT-1b` — behavioural replay from artifacts
alone in a transcript-free session — therefore remains untested.** A gated stage is not evidence of
a proven orchestration capability. State the transport in every verification record and gate commit.

### 13.7 Hard stops that remain the human's

Autonomy must not silently swallow these. The Owner **stops**, states its recommendation, and names
the action sequence that fires on approval (§13.2):

1. **Architectural model decisions** — a change to the computational model, not an implementation choice.
2. **Epic sequencing and stage insertion** — what gets built and in what order.
3. **Harness and config changes** — `.claude/settings.json` and anything that alters how the harness itself runs (`HOOK-1`).
4. **Adoption decisions with blast radius** — e.g. `L-6`, where enabling a gate rejects the existing corpus.
5. **A fourth Builder round** (`TERM-1`) — and any exception to a register constraint.
6. **Changes to this Owner Contract** — the control plane is never edited by the process it governs
   while that process is running (`FREEZE-1`).

Everything not on this list — routine progression, dispatch, rework within the cap, gating on
independent proof, merging, register bookkeeping — is the **Owner's** to execute without asking.

### 13.7a Architectural Proposal Contract (`EVIDENCE-1`) — mandatory

**Every architectural proposal — the Owner's, a reviewer's, or the human's — MUST carry all seven
fields. A proposal missing any of them is not a finding; it is an opinion, and it may not be
sequenced, adopted or cited as support for another proposal.**

| Field | What it must contain |
|---|---|
| **Evidence** | The observation itself: a command and its output, a `file:line`, an incident. Not an argument about what *would* happen |
| **Confidence grade** | `EVIDENCED` · `PARTIALLY EVIDENCED` · `HYPOTHESIS` · `UNEVIDENCED (preventive)` · `REASONING, NOT EVIDENCE` |
| **Operational incidents** | The real occurrences, named and dated. "None" is a valid and important answer — a preventive control with zero incidents must say so |
| **Sample size** | The actual `n`. Sessions, runs, stages. `n=1` is reportable; `n=1` presented without the number is not |
| **Alternative explanations** | The competing causes that would explain the same evidence, **including ones that argue against the proposal.** A proposal whose author found no alternative has not looked |
| **Recommendation** | The smallest change that would settle or fix it — not the largest change it would justify |
| **Priority** | Tier A/B/C/D plus an ordinal, with dependencies named |

**Why this is a contract and not a style guide.** The framework holds Builders to "a claim is not
evidence" (`L-7`) and holds register rows to "a live defect carries a reproduction" (`ATTRIB-1`), and
then accepted architecture proposals on argument alone. On 2026-07-22 the Owner cited *"shorter
sessions fail less"* in an architecture review from **three data points** with duration, token volume
and API load all uncontrolled. It read as a finding. It was a pattern the author liked.

**A hypothesis may be scoped, sequenced and prepared. It may not be ADOPTED until its grade
improves**, and the grade improves only through new observation — never through restatement.

**Objective trigger:** any proposal lacking a field, or citing a graded-below-`EVIDENCED` item as
support for another proposal, is in violation.

### 13.7b Governance Model (`GOV-1`) — the finalised principles

Six principles, each already carried by a named row; consolidated here so the governance model is
stated in one place rather than re-derived. **This section is a map, not new law** — it points at the
enforcing artifacts.

1. **The adversarial checklist is Verifier methodology, not Builder guidance** (`ADVERSARIAL-CHECKLIST-1`).
   Classes of attack, never expected defects; never a Builder pass-list; explicitly non-exhaustive
   (`VER-2` still governs scope).
2. **Every checklist class requires a constructive outcome** — an artifact that should-fail-but-passed,
   or "attacked, could not construct one." **Silence is not coverage** (`ADVERSARIAL-CHECKLIST-1`).
3. **Actor independence is fixed by the Decision Authority Matrix** (`.ai/contracts/decision_authority.md`):
   `BLD` implements · `VER` attempts to defeat · `OWN` classifies and dispatches · `CP` enforces
   lifecycle, accounting, retries, transitions, completion. **No responsibility migrates without an
   architectural justification recorded under `EVIDENCE-1`.**
4. **The Decision Authority Matrix exists** and is corpus-validated (`decision_authority.md`,
   `DECISION-AUTHORITY-MATRIX`). It becomes *enforced* — a validator checking the acting actor against
   the authorised one — only after the control plane stabilises.
5. **Deterministic enforcement is separated from semantic judgment** (`PLANE-1`): a decision
   expressible as a deterministic invariant belongs to `CP`, not the Owner. Owner judgment is reserved
   for the semantic four — FIX/DEFER, scope expansion, dispatch quality, progression *policy* (the
   *scheduling* of it moves to `CP` via `PROGRESS-TICK-1`).
6. **Framework evidence grading is mandatory** (`EVIDENCE-1`): every proposal carries operational
   evidence, confidence grade, sample size, alternative explanations, recommendation, priority. Grades:
   `Evidenced` · `Partially Evidenced` · `Hypothesis` · `Preventive` · `Reasoning` · `Withdrawn`.

**Corpus validation (principle 7), recorded not assumed:** the matrix found **D7 (progression)
misplaced to the Owner** (5 `PROG-1` stalls) and **D10 (epic-state write authority) asserted CP-only
but not enforced closed** (`WRITER-1`). Both are tracked findings, not new discoveries buried here.

### 13.8 External Stage Launch Contract (`LAUNCH-1`) — mandatory

> **External work is visible by default. The terminal is for observation; durable events are the
> canonical communication channel. The human is never the message transport.**

Established by human directive 2026-07-21, after the program's first real external dispatch ran as a
detached `PPID 1` process with no log, discoverable only because Claude Code happens to keep its own
transcript.

#### 13.8.0 The single canonical launch path (`CANON-1`)

**There is ONE launch path. An operator never chooses between execution paths per stage** — that
choice was itself the defect, and it is what `DISPATCH-2` recorded as three partial paths with
nothing saying which governs what.

> **The canonical continuation edge is `ai epic continue <epic>` (`CANONICAL-CONTINUE-RESOLVER-1`).**
> It closes the first-stage cold-start gap (`create → validate → seed/register → Owner-bound →`
> *no canonical progression edge* `→ model interprets "continue" → legacy /autopilot risk`). It is a
> **composition-only resolver**: it re-reads durable state, classifies the condition, and routes to
> exactly ONE existing sanctioned operation (`ai epic own next --execute` / `ai epic prepare` /
> `ai epic supervise`) or PARKs/COMPLETEs/RECOVERs — it never writes lifecycle, emits
> `stage.ready`/`execution.requested`, allocates, launches a Builder/Verifier, chooses a
> provider/transport, consumes a human gate, or (when `AUTONOMOUS_DISPATCH` is off) recommends a
> legacy path — it PARKs `PARK_CANONICAL_DISPATCH_DISABLED` instead. Post-seed activation
> (`seed --own` → `--after-seed`), recovery ADVANCE/START_NEW, `ai work <epic> --execute`, and the
> flag-gated post-DONE AUTOINVOKE all converge on this one resolver. It is acyclic w.r.t. recovery
> (it calls the read-only classifier `ai-recovery-resolve.sh`, never the executing router).

```
Owner prepares (spec with AC-ids + dispatch package)
  → dispatch-check green (PORT-1a)
  → seed (ROADMAP + CURRENT_STAGE)
  → dispatch against the PREPARED PACKAGE, in a visible terminal (§13.8.1)
  → Builder → independent Verifier → Gate → Merge
```

**Why prepared-package and not `/autopilot` self-generation — this is forced, not preferred.** The
entire `epic-stage-preparation-integrity` epic exists to make preparation a **gate**. Stage 5.1.6
certifies Builder-readiness against a certificate binding the Roadmap + Spec + Plan + Test +
Done-Criteria content hashes; `I21` binds a spec sha256; `dispatch-check` validates the package;

#### 13.8.1 The launch — two sanctioned forms, and only two

Every stage that executes in an external session launches in **exactly one** of these:

1. **Operator-visible terminal.** The Owner launches the Builder into a real terminal window the
   operator can watch and, in an emergency, interact with. On macOS:
   `osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script "…"'`.
2. **Operator-run command.** The Owner hands the human the **exact, complete command** and the human
   runs it — e.g. `ai auto <stage-id>`. The Owner shows the command **before** execution, never
   after.

**Prohibited: an unattended hidden session when a visible launch is available.** A headless launch is
permitted only under the §13.8.6 fallback, and only with the reason recorded.

**VISIBLE IS NOT OBSERVABLE (`LAUNCH-2`).** A window that opens and then shows nothing satisfies the
letter of a visible launch and none of its purpose. The first implementation did exactly that: it
ran `claude -p`, which is print/batch mode and buffers all output until the end, so the operator got
a banner and an empty screen.

**A launch is only complete when the terminal is a live execution monitor.** It must continuously
answer the operator's actual questions — *is it starting, reading, editing, testing, waiting,
stalled, or done?* — without the operator reading a transcript file by hand or attaching a second
client. Concretely it must show, as they happen: session start, a coarse phase label per action, an
**idle heartbeat** so "slow" is distinguishable from "stalled", and a terminal status line with the
exit result.

**Preferred source: the framework's durable execution events.** The terminal renders *events*, not
model transcript. **Today that source does not exist** — Builders emit no durable events and nothing
consumes the bus (`LAUNCH-1`, `LAUNCH-2`). Until 5.2.2 defines the Owner⇄Builder event contract, the
monitor renders progress **derived** from the session stream, and **must label it as derived on
screen.** Presenting inferred progress as canonical events would be the same false-claim pattern this
engine keeps finding in its own proofs.

#### 13.8.2 What the Owner records at launch

The launch is not complete until the Owner holds and records all of:

- the **execution id** (`exec.<epic>.<stage>[.aN]`),
- the **session id / transcript path** of the launched session,
- the **workspace** — worktree path, branch, base commit,
- the **transport** (`PROV-1`) and the **auth identity actually used** (`ENV-2`).

An execution whose output cannot be located from its own record is a defective launch, not an
inconvenience.

#### 13.8.3 Communication — durable events, not conversation

The Builder communicates with the Owner through the framework's **durable event/message channel**.
The Owner consumes those events, answers Builder questions, routes decisions, and continues the
workflow **automatically**.

**The human is never a message transport.** Copying text between an Owner session and a Builder
session by hand is a contract violation, not a workaround. The human is involved only when a **real
decision or approval** is required — the §13.7 list.

> **STATUS — PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, stated plainly rather than discovered later.**
> `.ai/orchestration/events/{pending,processing,completed,failed,dead-letter}/` exists **and is

> claim (`pending/`→`processing/`, exactly-once), and `ai-epic-dispatch.sh`,

> What remains absent is an **inbound channel to a *running* Builder session** — Builders do not
> emit progress events mid-execution, and the Owner cannot push a decision into a live session.
> **Until Stage 5.2.2 defines the Owner⇄Builder event contract, the Owner's interim mechanism for
> observing a running Builder is POLLING** — transcript, execution record, worktree state — and it
> must be *disclosed as polling*, never described as event routing. Building a private mailbox on
> the executor to close this early is forbidden: it would create the second, undocumented
> coordination path this epic exists to remove.

#### 13.8.4 Observation without interference

A running Builder is observed **read-only**:

```bash
tail -f ~/.claude/projects/<escaped-worktree-path>/<session-id>.jsonl
git -C <worktree> status --short          # what it has actually changed
ps -p <pid>                               # is it alive
```

**Never attach a second client to a live session** — `claude --resume <id>` against a running
execution puts two clients on a session that is actively writing, with no guard preventing it.
`--resume` is for **after** the process exits.

#### 13.8.4a Terminal-result handling (`ACTOR-FAILURE-1`) — the control plane, not the window

**The visible monitor is informational only. It is never the control-plane source of truth.**
Gate on the actor's canonical terminal result, consumed by `scripts/ai-actor-result.sh <run-dir>`.

**Actor SUCCESS requires all three; any disagreement fails closed:**

1. process exit code `0`,
2. the terminal result event carries no `is_error` / `api_error_status`,
3. the expected terminal artifact exists — the required verdict line is actually present
   (`--expect-verdict`).

**Infrastructure failure is a different class from a verification finding.** An API connection
closure, rate limit, overload or 5xx is **not** a `REWORK_REQUIRED`, **not** a completed round, and
**must not consume a `TERM-1` rework round**. Required handling: preserve the transcript and failure
record, retry automatically within the execution retry budget, escalate only when that budget is
exhausted or the failure is non-retryable.

**The retry policy (`scripts/ai-actor-retry.sh decide <epic> <stage> <run-dir>`) completes the
contract — classification without policy is half a contract:**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Retryable | `FAILURE_INFRA` only — API closure, rate limit, overload, 5xx, timeout, network |
| Never retryable | `FAILURE_ACTOR` (a real outcome) and `FAILURE_INDETERMINATE` — the actor may still be alive, and relaunching risks duplicating it onto the same worktree |
| Budget | `ACTOR_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES` (2) · `ACTOR_MAX_COST_USD` (60) · `ACTOR_MAX_WALL_MINUTES` (300) — env-overridable and **printed on every decision**, per the `WATCHDOG_GRACE_SECONDS` precedent `TERM-1` requires of any policy constant |
| Durable state | `.ai/orchestration/executions/retry.<epic>.<stage>.json` — in the registry that already survives restarts. **A counter held in a transcript is not a budget**; it resets on session loss, which makes an infinite retry loop across restarts the default failure mode of any in-memory design (`STATE-1`) |
| `TERM-1` interaction | `rounds_consumed` increments **only** on `SUCCESS`-with-verdict. `infra_attempts` is a separate counter. An attempt that produced no verdict is not a round, so infrastructure can never spend a stage's budget |
| Escalation | budget exhausted on any axis, or a non-retryable outcome → stop and hand the human the record |
| Reset | `reset --reason` is a **human** action and must be attributable; it clears the retry budget and **never** clears `rounds_consumed` |

Exit codes: `0` PROCEED · `10` RETRY · `11` ESCALATE. Operational Status must report the current
attempt and remaining budget while any retry is in flight.

Outcomes are distinct exit codes so that "could not evaluate" never reads as a substantive result:
`0` SUCCESS · `10` FAILURE_INFRA (retryable) · `11` FAILURE_ACTOR · `12` FAILURE_INDETERMINATE.

#### 13.8.5 Termination and recovery

If the process dies, the record does **not** self-correct — `active_execution()` reads
`registered`/`started` as live, so the stage stays "already active" and every retry is refused. The
sanctioned sequence:

```bash
bash scripts/ai-execution-watchdog.sh                       # scan: adjudicate → blocked/recoveryRequired
bash scripts/ai-execution-watchdog.sh resume <exec-id> --executor <the SAME executor>
```

**`--executor` is mandatory on resume.** It defaults to the standard executor, which runs
`/autopilot` — for a rework round that overwrites the stage spec and regresses `FINDING-F`
(`REWORK-1`). The safe path is one flag away from the destructive one, with no guard between them.

Nothing schedules the watchdog (`O3-LIMIT`); the Owner invokes it.

#### 13.8.6 Fallback ladder when a visible terminal is unavailable

In order. Each step is taken only when the one above it is impossible, and **the reason is recorded
in the execution record**:

1. Visible terminal (§13.8.1 form 1).
2. Operator-run command (§13.8.1 form 2) — preferred over any headless launch when a human is present.
3. Headless launch **with** a captured log — redirect the executor's output to a durable file and
   record its path. A headless run whose output is captured and discoverable is acceptable; one whose
   output is lost is not.
4. Refuse to launch. An execution nobody can observe and nobody can recover is worse than an
   unstarted one.

CI and other genuinely unattended contexts use step 3 by design, with `HEADLESS=1` stated explicitly
rather than inferred from the absence of a terminal.

| Artifact integrity gate | `ai-validate-artifact-integrity.sh` | Runs BEFORE Gemini, BEFORE exports are trusted |
| Promotion to canonical paths | `ai-promote-autopilot-artifacts.sh` | Only runs AFTER Gemini GO verdict |

**Enforcement:** `ai-architect.sh` auto-detects autopilot context via `AUTOPILOT_MODE` env var
and suppresses the interactive seed/reject prompt. If `ai-architect.sh` exits non-zero,
autopilot MUST stop — no exports written, no state created, no Gemini review.
Partial exports are deleted on failure.

## 2) Session Rules

### Scope Declaration (mandatory at session start)

```
Scope: [directories being modified]
Cross-repo impact: YES/NO
Boundary classification: [domain-only | internal | shared-api | shared-ui | cross-repo | event]
```

### One Stage Per Session

- Parallel stages = separate sessions
- Sequential stages = separate sessions
- Forbidden paths are hard boundaries — use spec, not code exploration
- Spec-first, not explore-first

### Closed-Loop Execution

Never pause to ask "shall I proceed?" — auto-continue until complete, max rounds, or error.

## 3) Git Discipline

- Branch naming: `feat/<short-name>` or `fix/<short-name>`
- Commit early and often
- Never force-push without human instruction
- Merge conflicts: STOP and report

## 4) Command Safety

### Never run destructive commands without human confirmation

`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fdx`, remote pushes.

### Architect Routing (which command to use)

| Need | Command | Why |
|------|---------|-----|
| Spec + plan generation (Phase A) | `ai architect --plan "topic"` | Loads templates, 12-20K context, artifact-ready output |
| Design question (full context) | `ai architect --full "question"` | 8-12K context, repo-aware |
| Quick architecture question | `ai architect "question"` | Light 4-8K context, advice only |
| Mid-execution question | `ai ask "question"` | Lightweight, no templates, keeps pipeline moving |
| Mid-execution + persist decision | `ai ask --save-decision "question"` | Saves to `.ai/decisions/` |
| Security/risk review | `ai ask --reviewer "question"` | Reviewer perspective |
| Formal checkpoint (scope change) | `ai architect request "topic"` | Produces `.ai/architect/decision_<topic>.md`, halts until resolved |

**Rule:** `ai ask` is for quick questions during implementation. `ai architect` is for anything that produces or informs artifacts (specs, plans, decisions).

### Other Delegation Commands

- `ai-memory.sh recall --type failure` — check past failures
- `ai-memory.sh record engine-defect "description"` — record engine bugs

### Embedded Architect Consultation

Auto-triggers when: multiple valid approaches + affects architecture/UX/API.
Does NOT trigger for: deterministic code, bug fixes, repo-grounded questions.

Flow: identify options → `ai architect "question"` → present unified answer → wait for human choice.

### Architect Checkpoint

Formal, persistent consultation for decisions that change scope/files/approach.
- Produces `.ai/architect/decision_<topic>.md`
- Halts implementation until resolved
- Check existing decisions before triggering new ones
- ALL decisions must be persisted as artifacts — never conversation-only

### Decision Enforcement Gate

Before generating stage artifacts: scan `.ai/architect/decision_*<topic>*.md`.
- Decision exists → seed from it directly. Do NOT re-call `ai ask`.
- Decision missing → use `ai architect` or trigger formal checkpoint.

## 5) Token Efficiency

### Repo Inspection Rules

- Default tools: Grep → Glob → Read (in that order)
- Max deep reads: 3-5 files per investigation
- Use scripts (`ai-validate-*`, `ai-sdui-audit`) for bulk analysis
- **DO NOT use Explore agents** for simple lookup or general questions
- Explore is blocked by hook — only allowed for `/explore-run` or `ALLOW_EXPLORE_AGENTS=true`

### Tool Priority: Grep → Glob → Read

Never spawn Explore for existence checks, repo inspection, or general questions.

### Budget Rule

If exploration:implementation ratio exceeds 3:1, stop exploring and start implementing.

### Response Rules

- Short confirmations only (changed files + status)
- No trailing summaries — the diff speaks
- No duplicate reads
- Verification output: status + duration + failures only
- Written artifacts: `updated <path>` + 3-line summary

| Gate | Script | When |
|------|--------|------|
| Pre-Gemini preflight | `ai-autopilot-preflight.sh <stage> --architect-exit $?` | After architect, before Gemini |
| Template sync | `ai-validate-template-sync.sh` | During preflight (Check 13) |

### What Scripts Check (you don't need to memorize)

### Canonical Pipeline Path (the ONLY valid execution order)

```
ROADMAP → architect exit 0 → write exports
  → preflight gate → Gemini review → promote
  → implement → self-tests → post-review
```

Anything outside this path is a hard stop.

### Failed Output Rules (engine-enforced by preflight gate)

1. **Never continue from failed tool output.** If `ai-architect.sh` exits non-zero, its output is untrusted. Discard it entirely.
2. **Discard, don't patch.** If architect output is malformed, delete exports and re-run after fixing the cause. Never manually edit spec/plan to fix architect failures.
3. **No patching spec/plan after failed architect output.** The preflight gate (Check 8) detects when architect exited non-zero but exports exist — this means someone patched manually. Hard stop.
4. **Regenerate only after fixing the cause.** If architect fails because of missing context, wrong template, or bad prompt — fix that first, then re-run clean.

## 11) Reviews & Packs

### Review Independence Invariant (GLOBAL)

**No agent may independently review an artifact it generated.**

| Phase | Author | Reviewers | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Phase B (brief review) | ChatGPT | Gemini + Claude | ChatGPT authored the brief |
| Phase D (plan review) | Claude | ChatGPT + Gemini | Claude authored the spec/plan |
| Phase G (post-review) | Claude | ChatGPT + Gemini | Claude implemented the code |

All review artifacts must include `ARTIFACT_AUTHOR:` and `REVIEWERS:` metadata.
Enforcement: `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` Gate 4e (review independence).

| Review | Owner | When |
|--------|-------|------|
| Conformance | Claude | Every stage |
| Boundary | Gemini | Cross-package work |
| Integration Gate | Claude | Multi-repo stages |
| Flow Validation | Claude | UI or cross-repo flows |
| Adversarial | Gemini + ChatGPT | Critical boundaries |

Optional packs (include when relevant): NFR, Security Audit, DevOps, ADR, Integration Gate, Evidence, UI Readiness, Flow Validation. Templates in `.ai/templates/`.

### Dual-Reviewer Decision Matrix

Only unanimous GO (plan review) or unanimous APPROVE (post-review) proceeds. All other combinations block.

| ChatGPT Verdict | Gemini Verdict | Pipeline Action |
|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| GO | GO | Proceed |
| GO | GO WITH CHANGES | BLOCK — patch + re-review |
| GO | NO-GO | BLOCK — fix issues |
| GO WITH CHANGES | Any | BLOCK — patch + re-review |
| NO-GO | Any | BLOCK — fix issues |
| APPROVE | APPROVE | Proceed (post-review) |
| Either CHANGES_NEEDED | Any | BLOCK — fix + re-review |
| Either REJECT | Any | BLOCK — fix + re-review |

Enforcement: `ai-autopilot-guard.sh` Gate 4d (plan review), Gate 4e (independence), and Gate 7a (post-review).
